4. Speed: Online voting can speed up the tallying process and generate results quicker than traditional paper-based voting.

1. Security risks: Online voting systems can be vulnerable to hacking, tampering or other forms of cyber-attacks, which could compromise the integrity of the election outcome.

2. Lack of anonymity: In some cases, online voting systems may not be able to guarantee anonymity, which could lead to coercion or intimidation of voters.

3. Limited access: Online voting may not be accessible to all voters, particularly those who lack the necessary technology or digital literacy skills to use the system.

4. Reliability: Technical issues or system failures could occur, which would hinder the ability of voters to cast their votes accurately.
